newsitem.title: USA: AT&T CFO sees no new local phone EPS impacts.
newsitem.headline: AT&T CFO sees no new local phone EPS impacts.

text.p: AT&T Corp has no plans to retreat from its long-term earnings targets, despite the slow start it and other long-distance companies have had entering U.S. local phone markets, its chief financial officer said.

In a phone interview, Dan Somers, who joined AT&T in May, said that, despite foot-dragging by the Baby Bells who dominate the local service business, AT&T does not anticipate any new impact on earnings from roadblocks to its local entry plans.
"There are no surprises here," Somers said, in noting that any impact its investments in local networks might have on earnings had been calculated in previously announced figures.

Somers contrasted AT&T's approach to local investments with rival MCI Communications Corp's headlong rush into local markets, which MCI recently said will lead to greater than expected losses for the rest of 1997 and 1998.

AT&T said in March that it expected 1997 year earnings in the range of $3.45 to $3.75 per share, but this would be cut by $0.75 to $1.00 per share by investments in new markets. More recently, AT&T has said the impact would be closer to $1.
The company had said at that time that these short-term investments would lead to higher long-term growth in the range of $5 to $6 by 2001.
"The impacts are the same and they have not changed," Somers said, referring to AT&T's previous guidance on the impact of investments to build out its local phone operations.

Somers said that, since becoming the financial overseer at AT&T, he has asked all operating units to take a tough look at their capital spending plans with an eye to reducing the overall amount of new capital spending this year.
AT&T said in March that it expected to spend between $8 and $9 billion in 1997 on new capital spending efforts, which in turn would hurt earnings for 1997 and in future years.

Earlier, in a conference call, Somers said the second quarter would represent the "low-water mark" in earnings results for the year. He also said he was confident AT&T could match the $0.64 per share consensus for the third quarter.
"That was the bottom. You will see improvements in both the third and fourth quarters," he said, although he noted the results will still be lower year-over-year.
The current Wall Street consensus earnings estimate for the fourth quarter is $0.63 per share.
